extracted.intended_audience: State, local, and Indian tribal governments and other recipients of U.S. Department of Education grants (grantees) required to follow OMB Circular A-87
extracted.subtask_description: Non-regulatory Department of Education guidance describing acceptable systems and standards for supporting charges to ED grants for salaries and related costs when employees work on multiple programs or cost objectives, including time distribution records, substitute systems, certification, monitoring, and consequences for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payroll documentation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges to an ED grant for salaries and wages must be based on payrolls documented in accordance with generally accepted practices of the recipient State or local agency and approved by a responsible official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payrolls must be supported by time and attendance or equivalent records for individual employees; salaries and wages of employees chargeable to more than one grant program or other cost objective must be supported by appropriate time distribution records; the method used should produce an equitable distribution of time and effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of system consistent with guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary accepts, for purposes of the time distribution records requirement, a system for supporting charges for salaries and related costs that is consistent with these guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These guidelines apply only to grants, cooperative agreements, and related subgrants made to or with entities governed by OMB Circular A-87 under programs for which the Secretary has administrative responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to support multi-program charges with time distribution or substitute
rubrics_metrics.description: If an employee works on more than one program or cost objective, a distribution of the employee's salaries or wages is acceptable if supported by time distribution records that meet the standards in paragraph (3) or by a statistical sampling system or other substitute system that meets paragraph (4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements regarding time distribution records systems are in addition to the standards for payroll documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time distribution records must reflect actual time (3)(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time distribution records must accurately reflect a distribution of the actual time spent on each activity by each employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department does not accept budget estimates or other distributions determined before the services are performed as support for charges to an ED grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time distribution records must account for total compensated activity (3)(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time distribution records must account for the total activity for which each employee is compensated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records should sum to the employee's total compensated time so all work is allocated among activities/cost objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemporaneous preparation and monthly summary (3)(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time distribution records must be prepared contemporaneously at least monthly and summarize the distribution of the employee's activity for the month in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly preparation is acceptable if the employee relies upon supporting documentation (calendars, class schedules, travel vouchers, work product) and entries are made to the best of the employee's knowledge and belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement (3)(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time distribution records must be signed by the employee or by a supervisory official who has first-hand knowledge of the activities performed by the employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signatures attest to the veracity and accuracy of the contemporaneous records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical employees: allowable methods (3)(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clerical employee time may be accounted for by basing records on the time distribution of the employee(s) they serve, with reasonable averaging where clerical staff serve multiple employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) Clerical serving a single employee may base time on that employee's time distribution. (ii) Clerical serving more than one employee may base records on the time distribution of each employee served, adjusted through use of a reasonable averaging method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable allocation when time cannot be divided (3)(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an employee's work benefits more than one program and the nature of the work makes dividing time impracticable, costs may be charged on a basis other than time provided charges are equitably distributed among funding sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include producing a single manual benefitting multiple grants (prorate by proportion of funds benefitting each grant) and teaching a mixed-class (prorate by proportion of students from each program). Justification for the method and the basis for cost allocation must be developed at adoption and maintained in records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of substitute systems and requirement for prior certification (4)(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may use a substitute system (e.g., statistical sampling, case counts) for allocating salaries and wages if, prior to charging Federal funds, it obtains certification from an independent public accounting firm or qualified auditor that the system is consistent with GAAP and standards in paragraph (4)(d) and provides equitable distribution of costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification must state the system employed and demonstrate that distribution is equitable to the government and programs, taking into account benefit actually derived by each program or cost objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification documentation and retention (4)(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The certification must describe the system employed and be available for inspection by the Secretary or designee; the certification and supporting documentation are subject to applicable record retention requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporting documentation upon which the certification was based must be retained and available for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible substitute system types and considerations (4)(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substitute systems may include random sampling, case counts, client counts, transaction counts, or other quantifiable measures of employee effort for a time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sampling and other measures should take into account relative effort or intensity of service between different categories of clients served; substitute systems must provide a quantifiable, equitable allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical sampling minimum standards (4)(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute system using sampling must meet acceptable statistical sampling standards, including: (i) universe includes all employees whose salaries are allocated; (ii) entire time period covered; (iii) results are statistically valid and applied only to the covered period; (iv) results periodically updated to reflect measure changes; (v) a valid, uniform system for converting measures into time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure sampling designs, extrapolation periods, and conversion methods are statistically defensible and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence restriction on certifying auditor (4)(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: A public accounting firm or qualified auditor that provided certification for a substitute system may not also audit that certification or the system in connection with an organization-wide or single audit under OMB Circular A-128.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves auditor independence and prevents conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written requests for Department guidance (5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A State or local educational agency with questions about its time distribution system or allowability of expenditures may write to the U.S. Department of Education for guidance pursuant to section 453 of the General Education Provisions Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written guidance reasonably relied upon by a recipient may be used to reduce or eliminate liability for a future finding of unallowable expenditures; see Section 453 and 34 C.F.R. 81.23.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and audit of systems (6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems of keeping time distribution records described in paragraph (3) or an approved substitute system are subject to monitoring and subsequent audit to ensure proper implementation and functioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Department reviews a bona fide certified substitute system, it may provide further guidance or direction but will not question prior costs incurred in accordance with proper implementation of a certified substitute system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional standards for certifying auditors (7)
rubrics_metrics.description: An independent public accounting firm or qualified auditor providing certification must use due professional care and operate within standards of professional ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department will take appropriate steps to ensure adherence to these professional standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for failure to meet time distribution requirements (8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a grantee fails to keep required time distribution records or to establish and maintain an approved substitute system, the Department takes an audit exception and recovers funds proportionate to the harm to an identifiable Federal interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grantee failing to keep records or maintain a satisfactory system is subject to audit and potential recovery of funds (see 20 U.S.C. 1234b(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-exclusive acceptable approaches and continuing review (9)
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidelines present acceptable but not exclusive approaches; compliance with these guidelines is regarded by Department officials as compliance with Circular A-87's time distribution requirement, but recipients may adopt other alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department will closely review the operation of this non-regulatory guidance to ensure it affords both accountability and flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and applicability (10)
rubrics_metrics.description: These guidelines are effective on issuance and are applicable to pending cases except where an advance certification is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should note the immediate applicability and any exceptions for advance certifications.
